problems.form_value: Individual-contributor strategy consultants at Boston Consulting Group, about 7 percent of the firm's global individual-contributor cohort
problems.source_says: The paper gives the 7 percent share for all 758 completers across both experiments, not for S1. S1 holds 385 of the 758, about half of that share, and the paper gives no share for S1 alone. The field should credit the share to the 758 (for example 'drawn from the 758 completers of both experiments, about 7 percent of the cohort') or drop it.
problems.quote: The pre-registered experiment involved 758 consultants comprising about 7% of the individual contributor-level consultants at the company.
problems.locator: PDF p. 4, Abstract; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 5), Section 2, second paragraph (same 7 percent for the whole experiment); PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6), 385 and 373 split

confirmed.statement: Enrollment and attrition: 852 consultants answered the enrollment survey and 758 (about 89 percent) completed the experiment, so 94 dropped out. The paper does not say whether the 94 had been randomized, or to which experiment or arm. With no count at assignment, n_randomized = null in S1 and S2 follows form-spec rule 1.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 5), fn. 3; PDF p. 10 (stratification uses the phase-one survey data); PDF p. 11 (assignment to conditions after the baseline task)

confirmed.statement: The 758 completers were allocated to two experiments 'with no overlap between the groups': 385 consultants in the inside-the-frontier experiment (S1) and 373 in the outside-the-frontier experiment (S2). 385 + 373 = 758, the abstract's total.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6), Section 2; PDF p. 4, Abstract

confirmed.statement: Individuals were randomly assigned to Control, GPT Only, or GPT + Overview after a no-AI baseline task, with stratification on gender, location, tenure, openness to innovation, and native English. The same three conditions apply in both experiments.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6); PDF p. 11 (printed p. 7)

confirmed.statement: S1 analyzed 385 people. Tables 1, 2, and 3 print Observations 385 in every column. The observations equal the 385 consultants, the dependent variables are per-subject measures (mean quality, completion share, time), and no S1 exclusion is reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 38-40 (printed pp. 34-36), Tables 1-3 and notes

confirmed.statement: S2 analyzed 373 people in Tables 4 and 5 and 372 in Table 6, which splits into 105 incorrect and 267 correct answers in cols (3)-(4). The paper does not explain the one missing person. The form records all three counts.

No count by arm appears anywhere. No table row, figure label, legend, or note gives N per condition (Figures 2 and 5-8, Appendix C Figures 1-3, Appendix D Figure 1). Arm-level n_randomized and n_analyzed = null are right.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 32-37, Figures 2-8; PDF pp. 38-43, Tables 1-6; PDF pp. 49-53, Appendices C-D

confirmed.statement: Appendix E describes 244 consultants who used AI on the analytic task (S2). The number pools the AI arms, does not split them, and the text does not say it covers every AI-arm subject. It cannot fill an arm count without inference, and the form keeps it in notes only.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 55, Appendix E, first paragraph

confirmed.statement: The counts are people. The paper counts consultants, and every table observation is a participant. Non-person units stay out of the people counts: the 100 simulated ChatGPT sessions ('GPT No Humans') are coded unit output with n_units 100 (S1-O5), and each subject's roughly 10 ideas are averaged into one subject-level similarity score.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 36, Figure 6 notes; PDF p. 52, Appendix D

confirmed.statement: The paper does not state how many subjects enter the similarity analysis (Figure 6, Appendix D Figure 1) or the idea-list creativity ratings, whose cited 'Table 1' is not in the PDF. The form says so.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16 (printed p. 12); PDF p. 36, Figure 6; PDF pp. 52-53, Appendix D

confirmed.statement: No person is in both studies. Within each study the same people did the no-AI assessment task and then the experimental task. The form uses this only for the Figure 5 before_after contrast, which it labels as not randomized.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6); PDF p. 11 (printed p. 7); PDF p. 35, Figure 5

confirmed.statement: The PDF names no other paper that analyzes these participants. Footnote 4 cites Dell'Acqua et al. (2023) only for a comparable assessment framework. No other screening candidate mentions BCG, and c052 (The Cybernetic Teammate) is a separate teamwork experiment, so a blank sample_overlap is right.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, fn. 4; PDF p. 26, References; candidates.json (c051, c052)

confirmed.statement: The population and country fields match for S1 and S2: individual-contributor consultants in BCG offices around the world. The only location variable is a binary Europe or Middle East control, so no country breakdown exists.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 5); PDF p. 15 (printed p. 11), fn. 9

confirmed.statement: The S1 and S2 participants quotes are verbatim on PDF p. 10.
Criterion 2 holds on S1 alone: 385 people analyzed across its three arms. S2 alone has 373.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10 (printed p. 6); PDF p. 38, Table 1; PDF p. 41, Table 4

summary: The PDF supports every participant count in the form: 852 enrolled and 758 completed (fn. 3, PDF p. 9), split with no overlap into 385 in S1 (Observations 385 in Tables 1-3) and 373 in S2 (373 in Tables 4-5, 372 in Table 6), and no count at assignment or by arm is printed anywhere, so the nulls are right and S1 alone clears 50 people. The one error is in S1's who field, which gives S1's 385 consultants the share 'about 7 percent of the cohort' that the paper gives for all 758 completers across both experiments.
